title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Renames that stay in scope, imports that stay
summary: Three renames that broke the build (a local leaking past its function, a Compose named argument, a class imported under an alias), an Organize Imports that removed the import behind `by remember`, soft keywords like `data` and `value` as identifiers, and smaller fixes in auto-import and postfix completion.

highlights.title: Local rename stays in its function
highlights.description: Renaming the `val user` of `load()` also rewrote `show(user: User)` and `this.user` further down the class. The scan ends at the closing brace now. A parameter rename updates `title =` at the call sites and no longer touches `TopAppBar(\n title = …)`.

highlights.title: Organize Imports keeps getValue
highlights.description: `import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue` / `setValue` and operator imports (`plus`, `component1`) are resolved by convention and never spelled in the file. The action removed them and every `by remember` stopped compiling.

highlights.title: data, value, actual are identifiers
highlights.description: `val data: T`, `val value: String` and `assertEquals(expected, actual)` were treated as keywords: only `?.data` counted, F2 on `value` did nothing. Declarations and plain uses count now; `data class` and `actual fun` still do not.

sections.heading: Rename and Find Usages
bullets: A local rename ends at the function's closing brace and skips `this.x` member accesses.
A parameter rename updates `name =` labels at call sites (file, and workspace when the function name is unique); a multi-line named argument of another call is not a usage.
A file importing the renamed class under an alias keeps its own bare `User`.
A one-line expression body (`fun Int.dp() = this * 2`) no longer claims the class below it as its body.
F2 on the first letter of a local `val` stays local instead of renaming the workspace.

sections.heading: Imports and completion
bullets: Organize Imports keeps convention-resolved imports (`getValue`, `setValue`, operators).
No "Add import" for a name already imported from a library (`material3.Text`).
`"Hello $name".let` keeps the whole literal as receiver and escapes `$` in the snippet.
Java import lines with `;` are organized and the auto-import lands inside the block.
